title: Stack Overflow / Q&A Platform
description: Design a Q&A platform where users post questions, write answers, vote on content, earn reputation, and tag questions. A **domain-modeling-heavy** problem that tests your ability to handle complex entity relationships and business rules (reputation thresholds, vote mechanics, accept answers).
prompt: Design a Stack Overflow-like Q&A platform where users post questions, write answers, vote, and earn reputation.
prompt_note: This problem is **domain-heavy, not algorithm-heavy.** The challenge isn't concurrency or data structures — it's modeling the rich entity relationships (User → Question → Answer → Vote → Comment → Tag) and the business rules that connect them (reputation thresholds, vote karma, accept answer bonus, badge criteria). Keep the design clean — resist the urge to put all logic in a single service class.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Core features — questions, answers, votes, comments, tags. Anything else?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Add reputation system. Users earn rep from upvotes, bounties, accepted answers. Reputation unlocks privileges (e.g., 15 rep to upvote, 125 to downvote, 2000 to edit others' posts)."
clarifying_questions.why: Reputation is the most interesting design element — it's a stateful computed value derived from user activity.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Voting mechanics — upvote/downvote on both questions and answers?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Yes. Upvote = +10 rep for author (+5 for question). Downvote = -2 rep for author, -1 for the voter (anti-abuse). A user can change their vote."
clarifying_questions.why: Vote-change means a vote is mutable state — not just an append-only event.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Can the question asker accept one answer? What's the rep bonus?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Yes — only the asker can accept. +15 rep for the answer author, +2 for the asker."
clarifying_questions.why: Accept is a special relationship: one accepted answer per question.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Search by tags, title, or content?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Tag-based filtering is core. Full-text search is out of scope."
clarifying_questions.why: Tag filtering = simple map lookup. Full-text search = Elasticsearch territory — HLD, not LLD.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Comments on questions and answers?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Yes, threaded comments. Keep them simple — no nested comments."
clarifying_questions.why: Comments are flat per post (question or answer). No deep nesting.

clarifying_questions.question: You: "Close / delete / edit questions?"
clarifying_questions.answer: Interviewer: "Edit yes (with reputation check). Close/delete are moderation features — mention but don't implement."
clarifying_questions.why: Keeps scope focused on CRUD + reputation.

core: **Users:** register, login (simplified), view profile with reputation and activity.
**Questions:** create (with tags), view, edit (rep check), list by tag / by date.
**Answers:** post answer to a question, edit, accept (by question author only).
**Votes:** upvote/downvote on questions and answers. Change vote. Undo vote.
**Comments:** add flat comments to questions or answers.
**Tags:** create tags, assign to questions, filter questions by tag.
**Reputation:** computed from votes + accepted answers + bounties. Unlocks privileges at thresholds.
**Privileges:** 15 rep to upvote, 125 to downvote, 2000 to edit others' posts.
out_of_scope: Full-text search, bounty system (beyond basic mention), moderation/close votes, badges, notification system, markdown rendering.

core: **Consistent reputation:** rep must always reflect the sum of all rep events. Recomputable from history.
**Vote integrity:** a user can only vote once per post. Changing a vote reverses the old one first.
**Thread-safe vote operations:** concurrent votes on the same post must not corrupt counts.
out_of_scope: Distributed deployment, full-text indexing, real-time notifications, caching layer.

primary_scope: `askQuestion(userId, title, body, tags)` → create Question → return questionId
`postAnswer(userId, questionId, body)` → create Answer → link to Question → return answerId
`vote(userId, postId, voteType)` → validate rep threshold → record vote → update author rep
`acceptAnswer(userId, answerId)` → validate asker → mark accepted → update rep
`addComment(userId, postId, body)` → create Comment → link to post
termination_points: `InsufficientReputationException` — user lacks rep to perform action (vote, edit)
`DuplicateVoteException` — user already voted on this post (offer change instead)
`SelfVoteException` — user tries to vote on own post
`NotQuestionAuthorException` — non-asker tries to accept an answer
`AlreadyAcceptedException` — question already has an accepted answer (allow changing)
entity_intro: This is the most entity-rich problem in the set. The entities are: User, Question, Answer, Vote, Comment, Tag. The interesting business rules live in the **relationships** between them — voting affects reputation, accepting affects reputation, reputation gates privileges.

entities.name: User
entities.role: **Model.** userId, displayName, email, reputation (long), createdAt. Reputation is recomputable from rep events but cached for fast privilege checks.

entities.name: Post (abstract)
entities.role: **Abstract base.** Shared by Question and Answer: postId, authorId, body, createdAt, voteScore. Questions and Answers both have votes and comments — shared via Post.
entities.verdict_label: ✓ Abstract — shared by Question and Answer

entities.name: Question (extends Post)
entities.role: **Model.** title, tags, acceptedAnswerId, answerCount, viewCount. A Question 'has many' Answers and 'has many' Tags.

entities.name: Answer (extends Post)
entities.role: **Model.** questionId, isAccepted. An Answer belongs to one Question.

entities.name: Vote
entities.role: **Model.** voteId, userId, postId, voteType (UP/DOWN), createdAt. Unique constraint: (userId, postId) — one vote per user per post. Mutable: user can change or undo.

entities.name: Comment
entities.role: **Model.** commentId, userId, postId, body, createdAt. Flat — not nested.

entities.name: Tag
entities.role: **Model.** tagName (PK), description, usageCount. Tags are reusable across questions. Many-to-many with Question.

entities.name: ReputationService
entities.role: **Service.** Centralizes rep calculations. `addRep(userId, amount, reason)`. Checks privilege thresholds. Maintains the running rep total.

entities.name: QnAService
entities.role: **Controller.** Public API: ask, answer, vote, accept, comment. Orchestrates all entities.

relationships.rel: N→1 User, N→1 Post. Unique: (userId, postId)

mvc_note: **MVC Mapping:** **Model** = User, Post, Question, Answer, Vote, Comment, Tag, VoteType enum, Privilege enum. **Service** = ReputationService (rep calculation + privilege checks), VoteService (vote mechanics + score updates). **Controller** = QnAService (the public API facade). The abstract Post base saves duplication — voting, commenting, and scoring work identically for Questions and Answers.
schema_note: **Single-table inheritance for Posts:** questions and answers in one `posts` table differentiated by `post_type`. Answers point to their question via `parent_id`. `votes` has composite PK `(user_id, post_id)` enforcing one-vote-per-user-per-post at the DB level. `reputation_events` is the audit log — user.reputation is a cached sum, recomputable via `SUM(delta) GROUP BY user_id`.

code_sections.label: Full Implementation — Model + Service + Controller (concise)
code_sections.flow:
**Vote flow:** check rep threshold → check not self-vote → check existing vote → if changing vote, reverse old delta first → apply new vote → update post score + author rep.
**Accept answer flow:** check user is question author → if already accepted, unmark old → mark new → update rep for both authors.
code_sections.edge_cases: Self-vote → rejected. Downvote costs the voter 1 rep. Changing upvote to downvote → reverse +10, apply -2 = net -12 for author, +1-1=0 for voter. Accepting a different answer → un-accept old (reverse +15), accept new (+15). User deletes account → votes remain but rep frozen.

patterns.name: Abstract Base → Post (Question + Answer)
patterns.why: Questions and Answers both have: author, body, voteScore, comments, createdAt. Extracting a `Post` abstract class eliminates duplication. `vote()` and `addComment()` work on any Post — they don't need to know if it's a Question or Answer. Classic polymorphism.

patterns.name: Observer Pattern (natural extension)
patterns.why: When someone answers a question, the asker should be notified. When someone comments, the post author should be notified. Votes trigger reputation changes that could unlock badges. These are all event-driven — Observer Pattern (or an event bus) is the clean way to decouple. Not implemented but mentioned.
patterns.where: Would add `EventBus` that fires on vote/answer/accept/comment events

patterns.name: Reputation as Event Sourcing
patterns.why: The `reputation_events` table logs every rep change with delta + reason. `User.reputation` is a cached sum. If it drifts, recompute from events. This is Event Sourcing at a micro scale — the events are the truth, the current value is a projection.

concurrency.issue: Concurrent votes on the same post corrupting voteScore
concurrency.fix: `voteScore` is an `AtomicInteger`. `updateVoteScore(+1)` and `updateVoteScore(-1)` are lock-free CAS operations. Two concurrent upvotes both succeed, score increments correctly by 2.

concurrency.issue: Two users accept different answers on the same question simultaneously
concurrency.fix: The `acceptAnswer` method accesses `question.acceptedAnswerId` — which is `volatile`. But the read-check-write pattern isn't atomic. **Fix:** synchronize on the question instance inside `acceptAnswer`. Or use `compareAndSet` on an `AtomicReference<String>`.

concurrency.issue: Vote change race — user rapidly changes vote
concurrency.fix: `votes.put(voteKey, newVote)` is atomic on ConcurrentHashMap. Rapid changes: each change reverses the previous and applies the new. In the worst case (two concurrent change requests), one reverse+apply pair might interleave, but AtomicInteger on voteScore and synchronized reputation updates keep each individual operation correct.

deep_dives.question: Why use an abstract Post class instead of two separate Question and Answer classes?
deep_dives.answer: **DRY + polymorphism.** Without Post: voting code duplicated (one for questions, one for answers). Comment code duplicated. Score tracking duplicated. With Post: `vote(postId)` works on any post. `findPost` returns a Post. The caller doesn't need to know the type. This is the **Liskov Substitution Principle** in practice.

deep_dives.question: How do you prevent a user from gaming the reputation system?
deep_dives.answer: **Voting ring detection:** if user A and user B consistently upvote each other, flag for review. **Daily rep cap:** Stack Overflow caps rep at 200/day from votes (accepted answers are uncapped). **Sockpuppet detection:** same IP, similar usernames, always voting for each other → automatic flag. These are all **moderation features** — mention as extensions.

deep_dives.question: Why is the downvote cost (-1 to voter) important?
deep_dives.answer: **Anti-abuse mechanism.** Without cost, users would mass-downvote competitors. The -1 rep cost means downvoting is a **costly signal** — you only downvote when you genuinely think the content is bad. Stack Overflow found this dramatically reduced revenge downvoting. **Game theory** applied to community moderation.

deep_dives.question: How would you implement tag autocomplete?
deep_dives.answer: **Trie (prefix tree)** on tag names. As the user types, traverse the trie to find all tags matching the prefix. Return top N by usage count. For LLD: a simple `TreeMap<tagName, Tag>` with `subMap(prefix, prefix + Character.MAX_VALUE)` gives prefix search. For production: Elasticsearch `completion` suggester.

deep_dives.question: How does Stack Overflow handle deleted users' content?
deep_dives.answer: **Content is anonymized, not deleted.** Posts by a deleted user remain with author shown as 'user12345'. Votes remain. Reputation impact on others remains. The user's profile page returns 404. This preserves the Q&A knowledge base while respecting the user's right to leave. In our model: set `authorId` to a tombstone ID, don't cascade-delete posts.

deep_dives.question: How would you add a bounty system?
deep_dives.answer: **Bounty entity:** asker deducts N rep from their own account (escrow) and attaches it to a question. After 7 days, the bounty auto-awards to the highest-voted answer (or is returned if no answers). The bounty creates two rep events: -N for the asker immediately, +N for the winner at resolution. Add a `BountyService` with a scheduled resolution job. The `Question` gets a `bountyAmount` field and `bountyExpiresAt` timestamp.
